title: Preserve the cursor shape during drag-n-drop
body:
We would like to add a new boolean attribute in DataTransfer to prevent it from overwriting the page's cursor during drag-and-drop operations.

Before creating a pull request for this, we'd like to get some general feedback about the proposed solution and/or alternative approaches we may not have considered.

### Background

When a page handles drag and drop events, the cursor is automatically set to one of the predefined drag cursors while the drag operation is happening. But this behavior is not always desirable. Web pages that explicitly set the cursor image are likely to want that image to remain in effect during the drag.

Demo: https://codepen.io/garykac/pen/yLEwLyJ

### Use case

An app that needs to set the cursor based on criteria other than what the browser thinks is being dragged and dropped.  In our specific case or a web-based remote access client, we need to set the cursor based on the remote machine's drag-n-drop operation, and ignore what the client thinks is going on. Imagine a web client connecting to Photoshop running on a remote machine - we need to preserve the remote cursor shapes when the user is clicking, dragging and drawing.

For the single window case, we can simply ignore the entire drag and drop API and just send the cursor events to the remote machine. However, we are now adding support for multiple local client windows (e.g., one local window per remote display) and these cursor events are only sent to the window where the mousedown/drag begins. In order to have a coherent drag from one window to another, we need to use the DataTransfer API (which as mentioned earlier, overwrites the cursor).

This API would work fine for this use case if only it didn't overwrite the current cursor. Hence this proposal.

### Current DataTransfer interface

The current DataTransfer interface has two attributes that affect the cursor while dragging:

```
partial interface DataTransfer {
	attribute DOMString dropEffect;
	attribute DOMString effectAllowed;
};
```
See https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#the-datatransfer-interface

The ```effectAllowed``` attribute controls which dropEffects are allowed. It can be set to "none", "copy", "copyLink", "copyMove", "link", "linkMove", "move", "all", or "uninitialized".

The ```dropEffect``` attribute controls the feedback that the user receives (i.e., the cursor shape). The possible values are "none", "copy", "link", and "move".

### Proposed Solution

We think the most reasonable way to address this would be to add a new attribute to DataTransfer:

```
partial interface DataTransfer {
	attribute boolean autoSetDragCursor = true;
};
```

This attribute would be set to true by default to match the current behavior of drag-n-drop, where the cursor is set automatically.

To use this attribute, it would need to be set in the ```dragstart``` event. If it is set to false, then the User Agent will not attempt to provide cursor feedback to the user during the drag.

### Alternatives Considered

We considered adding a new value to ```effectAllowed```, but felt that the current structure of this attribute is complex enough already that we shouldn't be adding more to it.

We also considered something analogous to ```setDragImage()```, but for setting the cursor image. However, since there are existing methods for setting the cursor it seems reasonable to just rely on them.

### Mitigating Abuse

This attribute would only be set in the ```dragstart``` event (when the [drag data store](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#drag-data-store)'s [mode](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#drag-data-store-mode) is read/write, just like the restriction for ```effectAllowed```).

The custom cursor is applied only within the content region, so the user cannot be tricked into dropping content outside the browser when they think they're dropping inside.

Setting a very large custom cursor that overlaps browser UI and other windows is not specific to drag-and-drop and has been addressed in the general case (by restricting max cursor size: see https://bugs.chromium.org/p/chromium/issues/detail?id=1246188).
